display.purpose: The one big figure per page (the price card's dollar amount), tabular.

headline.purpose: The page h1 on every page (the shared page header); on a broker page the broker's name.

headline-sm.purpose: A card heading that is itself an answer (About $9 a year).

title.purpose: Card headings; at 700 the rank line and, under it at the same size, the same-stock rank line (rank 700, words 500); at 600 the unit beside the big figure; the wordmark.

lead.purpose: The generated sentence under the scale, max 62ch.

body.purpose: Running text and row labels; values at 700, tabular.

label.purpose: Row sub-notes, table column headings, scale captions, footnotes; sentence case.

shadows.name: lift-dark
shadows.purpose: Every card and the current nav pill (dark).

shadows.name: pop
shadows.purpose: Menu panel; hover of a wholly pressable card (light).

shadows.name: pop-dark
shadows.purpose: Menu panel; hover of a wholly pressable card (dark).

shadows.name: press
shadows.purpose: Under teal fills: solid button, checked switch option (light).

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Every focusable element; white on a teal panel; on a wholly pressable card or table row the ring moves to the card or row.

motion.name: ease-out

motion.name: press

motion.name: scale-glide
motion.purpose: The scale's dot, tick and labels glide to their new places when the stock switch flips.

motion.name: table-rerank

motion.purpose: The ranked table re-sorts in place when the stock switch flips.

motion.name: chevron

motion.name: reduced-motion

narrative.overview:
Every page is one soft card stating one answer in plain words, laid on a pale ground tinted from the action teal. The system is a warm consumer app, not a trading dashboard: white cards with generous corners and a shadow you notice only as lift, Figtree for everything, the number first and set big, and a single teal that appears only on things you can press. Nothing on the page sells, celebrates or alarms. Meaning is carried by words ("above the fair price", "10th cheapest of 25", "Not confirmed"), never by a red or green figure.

Density is low and deliberate: one idea per card, cards stacked in columns, explanations one click away behind an (i) or a "How we measure" link. The product's signature is the neutral price scale, a grey rail that places one broker's ink dot between the cheapest and the most expensive with a tick at the typical broker, drawn in CSS and gliding when the stock switch flips. Every comparison that the scale summarises is also given as a real table.

Light is the default; dark follows the system until the visitor picks a theme, and both themes are tuned separately rather than auto-inverted. The world rejects gradients, glow, icon tiles, uppercase kickers, colour-coded verdicts, ratings and "Open account" buttons.
keyCharacteristics: Soft white cards (24px corners, 20px on phones) on a teal-tinted neutral ground (light page; in dark, a dim sage page with lighter cards).
One typeface, Figtree, weight 800 for headings and the big figure, tabular numerals for every number.
One action colour, teal, reserved for pressable things; everything else is ink and tinted greys.
The neutral price scale as the signature visual; tables for every comparison.
Pill-shaped controls, 44px minimum hit areas, a 3px teal focus ring clear of the element.
One motion curve, an exponential ease-out with no overshoot; nothing moves under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Press-Only Teal Rule
rules.body: Teal marks only what can be pressed or what has keyboard focus. A heading, a figure, a badge, a decorative shape or a "good" value is never teal. If it is teal, clicking it does something.

rules.name: The Words-Not-Colour Rule
rules.body: Good and bad are stated in words ("below the fair price", "11th cheapest of 20", "Not paid", "Pays $0.07 to its trading firm", "Not confirmed"), never by colouring a figure red or green. Outside the explorer a figure below its reference is said in words too ("$0.09 below", never "−$0.09"). Prices, ranks and payments are all ink.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: All text reaches at least 4.5:1 on its own background in both themes (light: ink-2 on surface 6.5:1, accent on surface 5.2:1, accent on page 4.6:1; dark: ink-2 on surface 8.0:1, accent on surface 7.7:1). Non-text marks reach at least 3:1 against the card (mark on surface 3.6:1 light, 5.6:1 dark). Text on Soft Teal is Deep Teal, never Action Teal (accent on accent-soft is 4.4:1 in light, below the floor).

rules.name: The Two Tuned Themes Rule
rules.body: Light and dark are each tuned by hand; in dark the teal lightens, the on-teal text turns near-black and hover goes lighter, not darker. The two dark blocks in the stylesheet (picked and system) stay identical.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every figure that can sit beside another figure (big amounts, table cells, fee values) uses tabular numerals.

rules.name: The No-Kicker Rule
rules.body: No uppercase eyebrows or letter-spaced labels above headings. A heading says what the card holds; a sub-line in secondary ink gives the scope and date.

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: No gradients, glows, coloured shadows or blurred backdrops. A shadow only says "this sits above the ground" or "this can be pressed".

dos: Do lead each page with one answer card: the figure at Display size, its unit in words beside it, then the rank and the scale.
Do keep teal for pressable things and focus rings only; use ink for every number and verdict.
Do state good or bad in words next to the figure ("above the fair price", "10th cheapest of 25").
Do pair every scale or ranked summary with a real table of all the brokers, the page's own row tinted Here.
Do keep text at 4.5:1 or more and marks at 3:1 or more in both themes; put Deep Teal, not Action Teal, on Soft Teal.
Do give every control a 44px minimum hit area and the 3px teal focus ring 3px clear.
Do use the one curve `cubic-bezier(.22, 1, .36, 1)` for every movement and turn all motion off under reduced motion.
Do name unknowns plainly ("Not confirmed", "Not offered", "Varies") in secondary ink.
Do let a select or switch only report a pick; anything that opens another page is a real link or button beside it.
Do open every page with the shared page header (Headline h1, at most one Lead-size intro line) and put a card's own control in its right-hand slot.
Do give every chart its table and its key in HTML, and draw rankings and scales in CSS rather than loading a chart library for them.
donts: Don't use gradients, glow, coloured shadows or the old gradient text and hero glow.
Don't put icons in coloured tiles; icons are line icons beside a word or the face of a round control.
Don't add uppercase, letter-spaced kickers or eyebrows above headings.
Don't colour figures red or green to mean good or bad, and don't colour the scale.
Don't add ratings, stars, badges, "Open account" buttons or cheerleading copy.
Don't build a dashboard of equal KPI tiles; one idea per card.
Don't introduce a second typeface or px font sizes outside the seven-step scale.
Don't use series colours outside charts and the routing heat table.
Don't make a table row a Tab stop; the row opens through the real link in its name.
Don't stick more than one short row to the top of a page.
